settingDescription: Hand-drawn historical 2D world of Boston's poor Italian and Irish waterfront district: brick tenements, cobblestone Commercial Street with the elevated railway on riveted steel girders, wooden warehouse sheds, harbor wharves, a brick firehouse and one huge riveted steel molasses tank painted brown.
recurringPlaces: Molasses tank: cylinder of riveted steel plates, as tall as a five-story tenement, painted brown after 1915, manhole cover at the base, valve pipe on the harbor side
Commercial Street: cobblestones, streetcar rails, elevated railway trestle on steel girders, horse wagons and early trucks
Firehouse 31: two-story brick building with an arched bay door and a horse-drawn fire engine
Tenement block: four-story brick houses with fire escapes, laundry lines and small porches
Hearing room: wood-paneled room with long tables, case files, tall windows
recurringCharacters: Isaac Gonzalez, Arthur Jell, Hugh Ogden, George Layhe and Bridget Clougherty exactly as defined in CAST_BIBLE.json
recurringProps: Large iron valve wheel at the back of the tank
Hardened brown molasses with a glossy surface, thick and sticky
timeWeatherLogic: 1915–1918 shown in mild seasons; 14 January 1919 freezing frost; 15 January 1919 sudden mild sunshine until the flood at 12:30, then cold afternoon; cleanup weeks later in winter; harbor still brown in summer 1919; court 1919–1925; epilogue today.
continuityRules: Recurring places keep their layout, but each return uses a different camera position or shot scale.
Show the tank intact until the narration reaches 12:30 on 15 January 1919; never show the wave, damage or ruins earlier.
Victims are shown with dignity: no visible bodies, no gore; loss is expressed through objects, absence and reactions.
Recurring people keep the identity text from CAST_BIBLE.json word for word.
